instructions: Assess the local method contract and its documentation. Check existing comments for factual contradictions, and whether a concrete, non-obvious assumption or intentional exception visible in the method needs a short explanation. Straightforward self-explanatory code does not need comments. Class documentation and inherited contracts count as explanation. Do not demand redundant narration or treat a missing callee, caller, runtime wiring or truncated evidence as a documentation defect. Comments are claims, not proof that callers enforce preconditions.

criteria.accurate: Existing factual claims agree with the visible implementation, or the method is self-explanatory and needs no additional comment.
criteria.contradicted: At least one factual claim conflicts with the code.
criteria.insufficient_context: The supplied implementation does not establish whether the claims hold.
criteria.needs_explanation: A concrete non-obvious precondition or intentional exception is visible in the code but unexplained by the method, class or inherited contract. A short contract comment would make local interpretation possible.
